messages.content:
Risk: Lack of transparency
Description: Challenges in understanding or explaining the decision-making processes of AI systems, which can lead to mistrust, difficulty in enforcing compliance standards or holding relevant actors accountable for harms, and the inability to identify and correct errors.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Decision Making

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#AlgorithmicDiscrimination: Algorithmic Discrimination — Systematic bias in automated decision-making systems that disadvantages specific groups based on protected characteristics. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: Employment Discrimination, Discriminatory Denial of Service, Housing Discrimination
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033071: Impaired task monitoring — Impaired ability to keep track of one's problem-solving success or failure, and to identify and correct mistakes during performance of a goal. [found by 6/15 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired ability to plan, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0033055: Impaired ability to plan — Impaired ability to anticipate future events, implement instructions or goals, and develop appropriate steps ahead of time in order to carry out a task or activity. [found by 5/15 queries]
  Siblings: Impaired task monitoring, Impaired self monitoring, Impaired ability to organize
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000146: Artificial Language — A Language that is developed through conscious planning and premeditation, rather than one that was developed through use and repetition. [found by 5/15 queries]
  Siblings: Natural Language
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 4/15 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party

axes.rationale: AI systems, due to their lack of transparency, may exhibit impaired task monitoring, struggling to identify and correct errors in their decision-making processes.
Lack of transparency in AI can contribute to algorithmic discrimination, as the reasons behind biased decisions may be difficult to discern and address.
